learningObjectives: Explain how Case Status communicates progress to users and reports
Identify the four Case Status categories and their naming conventions
Configure Instructions for a Task to guide users at runtime

elements.description: Case status communicates progress. It uses Work-.pyStatusWork; configured Rules and notifications may refer to it, but the value does not by itself guarantee a particular notification.

elements.text: Case status and assignment instructions are like a traffic light and GPS directions combined: the status indicator tells everyone where the case is in its journey (Open / Pending-Approval / Resolved), while the step instructions are turn-by-turn directions telling the current worker exactly what to do before pressing 'Submit.' Miss either one and the driver is left guessing at a green light.

elements.description: Four conventional Case status prefix categories:
items: Pending — waiting on something or someone
Resolved — processing is complete, with no remaining open Assignments; examples include Resolved-Completed and Resolved-Rejected

elements.description: Configure status at meaningful Stages or Steps. A configured transition updates status; the final Stage’s resolution status applies after its Processes complete. Not every transition needs a different status.

elements.caption: Status communicates progress; configured transition values and final resolution serve different points in the lifecycle.

elements.title: Case Status & Guidance Design Decisions

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Guiding users: instructions, help text, and visual cues

elements.description: Text added to a Collect-information Step/Assignment that tells the user exactly what they must do to complete the Task. Instructions render at runtime on the assignment form, reducing confusion and errors.
Additional text beside an input can clarify the expected value. Instruction text explains the task; neither replaces validation or authorization.
The Form can show the configured Step instructions, override them with task-specific text, or hide them. Choose guidance that helps the user complete the current Assignment.

examPitfalls.title: Status prefixes and closure
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions list Case Status values and ask which prefix signals closure. Candidates select 'Completed-' or 'Finished-.' Case Statuses that begin with 'Resolved-' signal closure — Pega uses this prefix to determine when a Case is considered done.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Remember: only the Resolved- prefix signals Case closure — Pending means waiting for something. Exam questions may list misleading prefixes like 'Completed-' or 'Finished-'.

examPitfalls.title: pyStatusWork
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A similarly named custom property is not the standard Case status property.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Work-.pyStatusWork when inspecting Case status; do not assume names without its prefix are equivalent.

examPitfalls.title: Status is set via the life cycle
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Automatic status updates occur when a Stage or Step with an explicit status configuration is reached.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure transition statuses at meaningful points; distinguish final resolution from entering the final Stage.

examPitfalls.title: Instructions guide the user at the Step
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where Instructions text appears to the user. Candidates say 'on the Case summary page.' Instructions are displayed at the Assignment level — they guide the user working on that specific Step, not on the overall Case summary.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Add concise instructions to each Assignment so users complete Tasks correctly.

examPitfalls.title: Status vs. Stage
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A Stage is a life-cycle phase; a status is a value describing where the Case stands. They are related but not the same.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Stage = phase of work; status = the reported state (can change within a Stage).

examPitfalls.title: Case status vs. Step label — different artifacts
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates conflate the status displayed in the case header (Case Status) with the step name shown in the process (Action name / Stage name).
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Status is a reported state; the Step name identifies the task. Configure transition statuses and instruction text for their distinct purposes.

examPitfalls.title: Assignment instructions are not case-level notes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks the correct way to communicate step-specific guidance to operators. Candidates describe adding a Note to the Case. Assignment Instructions are the correct tool — they are Step-specific and displayed only when the operator is working on that Assignment.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Provide task-specific instruction text at the active Form. A general Case discussion has a different purpose; Form configuration can override the Step text.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user filling out a loan application form needs to understand what value to enter in a 'Requested Loan Purpose' field. The SA wants to display a short description of accepted values directly below the field label. Which UI guidance mechanism should be used?

options.text: Field-level help text — a short description shown directly beneath the field label to guide the user on valid inputs
A Pulse comment — the SA adds a comment to the Case's Pulse stream that the user reads before filling out the field
A Case-wide tooltip — a single tooltip at the top of the form describes every field in the Case for the user
An email notification — the system sends an email to the user before they open the form describing what to enter

practiceQuiz.hint: Short description below a field label = field-level help text.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Field-level help text appears directly beneath or beside the field label, giving the user immediate, contextual guidance without leaving the form. Tooltips are on-demand (hover); section headers provide structural context.

optionExplanations.A: Field text supplies guidance where the user enters this value.
optionExplanations.B: A collaboration discussion is not positioned at the input field.
optionExplanations.C: A single generic hint does not supply the requested field-level context.
optionExplanations.D: An earlier email is less direct than guidance beside the current input.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A CSR searches for 'all closed loan applications from last quarter.' In the reporting filter, which status prefix should they use to find Cases that have reached the end of their life cycle?

options.text: 'Resolved-' — Cases with a status beginning with 'Resolved-' are closed; the system uses this prefix to distinguish closed Cases from active ones (New, Open, Pending)
'Closed-' — Pega uses 'Closed-' as the terminal status prefix; 'Resolved-' is used for intermediate escalation statuses
'Final-' — Case statuses ending the life cycle must begin with 'Final-' to trigger the Case closure mechanism in Pega
'Complete' — there is no required prefix; any status the team designates as terminal will automatically close the Case when set

practiceQuiz.hint: What prefix distinguishes a Case that has reached end-of-life from one that is mid-process?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Cases with status beginning 'Resolved-' are closed. The 'Resolved-' prefix is the standard Pega convention that identifies terminal-state Cases — any other prefix indicates an open Case.

optionExplanations.A: Resolved status identifies completed Case processing.
optionExplanations.B: Closed is not the standard resolution family described here.
optionExplanations.C: Final is not the standard resolution prefix.
optionExplanations.D: A generic completion label is not equivalent to the supported status semantics.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A report reads a custom StatusWork property instead of the standard Case status property. Which property should the SA inspect?

options.text: Work-.pyStatusWork — the standard property for Case status
pxStatusWork — all work status properties use this name
StatusWork — Pega automatically treats a missing prefix as equivalent
workStatus — the standard property was renamed and pyStatusWork is obsolete

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the exact standard property name.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Case status uses Work-.pyStatusWork. A similarly named custom property is not automatically equivalent.

optionExplanations.A: The exact standard work-status property is Work-.pyStatusWork.
optionExplanations.B: Changing the prefix changes the property being referenced.
optionExplanations.C: A similarly named property is not automatically the standard property.
optionExplanations.D: The scenario provides no basis for a renamed standard property.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Claims application needs active-review, approved and withdrawn statuses. Which set most clearly distinguishes active work from resolved outcomes?

options.text: Open-Review, Resolved-Approved and Resolved-Withdrawn
In Progress, Done and Closed with no distinction between active and resolved work
Open-Review, Completed and Finished as the resolution statuses
Start-Review, End-Approved and End-Withdrawn as the standard categories

practiceQuiz.hint: Pega uses 'New', 'Open-', and 'Resolved-' conventions. Which set follows all three?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use the standard status families and meaningful suffixes. Approved and withdrawn are alternative outcomes, not successive mandatory Stages.

optionExplanations.A: The active review is separated from the two terminal outcomes.
optionExplanations.B: Unqualified labels fail to communicate the standard distinction.
optionExplanations.C: These terminal labels do not use the standard resolved family.
optionExplanations.D: Start and End are not the standard families in the status table.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Form View needs different instructions from the default instructions configured on its Case Step. What supported configuration fits?

options.text: Override the Step instructions with custom text in the Form View
Add a Pulse post and assume it replaces Step instructions
Change the Case status to store the full instruction paragraph
Rename the Work Queue so its name becomes the Form instructions

practiceQuiz.hint: Form instruction configuration is distinct from Case status.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Form can show, override or hide the configured Step instructions. Keep instruction text separate from work status.

optionExplanations.A: The Form supports overriding the default Step instructions.
optionExplanations.B: A Pulse discussion does not replace configured Form instructions.
optionExplanations.C: Case status is a state value, not a container for instruction paragraphs.
optionExplanations.D: A queue name describes a routing destination, not task instructions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A business stakeholder asks the SA: 'How does Pega help users avoid entering a date in the wrong format?' Which built-in mechanism enforces this on the View?

options.text: Field-level validation — configuring a Date field type enforces the correct format automatically and shows an inline error if the format is wrong
A Data Page — the Data Page rejects incorrectly formatted dates before they reach the Case and returns a formatted value to the View
Channel configuration — the channel detects the user's locale and blocks incorrect date formats at the network layer before processing
A Case Life Cycle transition condition — the Stage transition checks the date format and refuses to advance the workflow if it is wrong

practiceQuiz.hint: Format enforcement on a form field = field-level validation (built-in on Date field type).
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use an appropriate Date field type and supported date control. Format checks do not replace business validation such as whether the date is in the future.

optionExplanations.A: Date metadata supports an appropriate input format and control.
optionExplanations.B: The source of records is not a universal date-format validator.
optionExplanations.C: The network channel does not define this field’s validation constraint.
optionExplanations.D: A Stage condition does not provide the field’s input-format control.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Collect information Step asks for a billing address. Users keep entering their shipping address. What guidance should the SA add?

options.text: Step instructions explicitly asking for the billing address associated with the payment method
A routing change that sends the task to a different Work Queue
A Ruleset name containing the words billing address
A resolved Case status before the user completes the form

practiceQuiz.hint: Provide guidance where the user enters the information.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Instructions explain the task at the point of input. They cannot guarantee valid data; use validation for enforceable constraints.

optionExplanations.A: Task instructions can clarify which address is required.
optionExplanations.B: Changing the assignee does not clarify the requested input.
optionExplanations.C: A technical package name is not visible task guidance.
optionExplanations.D: Resolving the Case before collecting input bypasses the task.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA proposes using an instruction paragraph to enforce a spending limit. What should the SA explain?

options.text: Instructions communicate the rule; validation or appropriate business Rules must enforce it
The instruction paragraph automatically prevents all excessive amounts
Instruction wording replaces the server-side validation configuration
The spending limit must be encoded in the Portal theme

practiceQuiz.rationale: Readable guidance helps users understand a requirement. Enforcement needs configured validation or business processing, not the text itself.

optionExplanations.A: Communicate the limit and separately configure its enforcement.
optionExplanations.B: Text alone does not implement a validation constraint.
optionExplanations.C: Natural-language guidance is not server validation configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Colors and fonts do not implement the spending rule.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An order Case has status Pending-Fulfillment. What does this communicate?

options.text: The Case is waiting for fulfillment-related work or an event
The Case is deleted and cannot be inspected
All processing is finished and the Case is resolved
The Case must have failed field-format validation

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the Pending category and its descriptive suffix.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pending indicates a wait; the suffix explains the context. It does not itself establish deletion or a validation failure.

optionExplanations.A: Pending plus its suffix describes the relevant wait.
optionExplanations.B: A wait status does not delete the Case.
optionExplanations.C: Pending is distinct from resolved processing.
optionExplanations.D: The status does not prove that any field validation failed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Users can already see an instruction paragraph in their Assignment form. What is its purpose?

options.text: Explain what they need to accomplish in this Assignment
Change the Case’s access-control permissions
Automatically fill every required field
Replace every validation Rule with natural-language text

practiceQuiz.hint: Guidance tells the user what to do.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Instructions guide the current task. Access permissions, default values and validation need their own configuration.

optionExplanations.A: The paragraph explains the current Assignment’s task.
optionExplanations.B: Instruction wording does not grant or remove privileges.
optionExplanations.C: Instructions do not automatically populate all input fields.
optionExplanations.D: Explaining a requirement does not implement its enforcement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Receipt Amount must not be negative. The error should be reported when the user submits the Form. Which approach fits?

options.text: Configure a validation condition with a clear error message for a negative amount
Hide the Stage label without validating the amount
Assume the Data Page rejects any negative number even without a configured constraint
Post a Pulse comment instead of preventing invalid submission

practiceQuiz.hint: Use a validation constraint and an actionable error message.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Submission validation can report invalid field values on the form. A notification or hidden label does not enforce the amount constraint.

optionExplanations.A: The constraint and error message identify invalid submitted input.
optionExplanations.B: A hidden label does not reject a negative amount.
optionExplanations.C: Data retrieval does not automatically enforce every business constraint.
optionExplanations.D: A discussion message does not prevent invalid submission.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Case enters an Investigation Stage with a configured Open-Investigation status. What happens?

options.text: The Case status updates to the configured value when the Case enters the Stage
The user must rename the Case manually for the status to change
Every open Assignment is deleted because the status begins with Open
The Stage is skipped because only Pending statuses can be used

practiceQuiz.hint: The Stage has an explicit status configuration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A configured Stage status applies when entering that Stage. Open indicates active processing, not resolution.

optionExplanations.A: The explicit Stage status applies at the transition.
optionExplanations.B: The configured update does not need a manual Case rename.
optionExplanations.C: Open describes active work and does not delete its Assignments.
optionExplanations.D: Active statuses can apply to Stages as well as waiting statuses.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A final Stage has resolution status Resolved-Completed. When should that resolution status describe the Case?

options.text: After the Processes in the final Stage complete
Immediately before any final-Stage Process has started
Whenever the user changes a tooltip label
Only when an administrator deletes the Case

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish entry status from the final resolution status.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The final Stage’s resolution status follows completion of its Processes. Entering a Stage and resolving the Case are distinct events.

optionExplanations.A: Resolution follows completion of the final Stage’s Processes.
optionExplanations.B: Entering a Stage does not mean all its work is already complete.
optionExplanations.C: Tooltip labels do not resolve workflow processing.
optionExplanations.D: Resolution and deletion are different operations.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer is setting up Case Statuses for a new Claims application. Which TWO of the following are valid Pega Case Status category prefixes?

options.text: Open-
Resolved-
Active-
Completed-

practiceQuiz.hint: Pega defines specific status category prefixes — recall the four standard categories, not custom naming.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Open and Resolved are standard status families. The standard table also includes New and Pending; Active and Completed are not substitutes for these category names.

optionExplanations.A: Open is the standard active-processing family.
optionExplanations.B: Resolved is the standard completed-processing family.
optionExplanations.C: Active is not the category named in the standard table.
optionExplanations.D: Completed is a possible outcome description, not the category prefix.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is designing user guidance for a multi-step Claims process in Pega Constellation. Which TWO elements provide in-context guidance to users completing an Assignment?

options.text: Instructions text configured for the Assignment Step
Additional text configured alongside the relevant input field
Audit history entries that describe past events rather than the current task
An urgency score indicating routing priority rather than what to enter

practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on elements shown to the user while they are actively completing a step, not after the fact.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Step instructions and contextual field text help with the current task. Historical events and urgency have different roles.

optionExplanations.A: Step instructions explain the current input task.
optionExplanations.B: Additional text supplies context beside the relevant input.
optionExplanations.C: Past events do not directly describe what to enter now.
optionExplanations.D: Priority does not explain the current field requirements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA wants to understand Case Status behavior in Pega. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Case Status communicates progress?

options.text: Case status communicates progress through the Case life cycle
A configured Stage or Step status is applied automatically at that transition
Case status is inherently restricted to administrators
Users must always edit status manually at every Step

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about what Case Status is designed to communicate and whether it updates automatically.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Status communicates progress. Automatic transition updates use the status configured for the Stage or Step; every transition need not have a distinct status.

optionExplanations.A: The status communicates the Case’s current progress.
optionExplanations.B: An explicitly configured transition can update status automatically.
optionExplanations.C: User guidance is not inherently an administrator-only feature.
optionExplanations.D: Manual editing is not required for configured transition updates.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is reviewing Case Status values configured in a Pega Claims application. Which TWO statements describe the correct naming convention for Case Status?

options.text: The standard status table includes New, Open, Pending and Resolved
A descriptive suffix can clarify a status such as Open-Investigation or Resolved-Withdrawn
Any invented prefix automatically carries the same resolution semantics
Every status must begin with the application name

practiceQuiz.hint: Check the standard table, including the initial New status.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use standard status families and meaningful suffixes. New is a standard initial status; Reserved is not the fourth category in this table.

optionExplanations.A: New is included alongside Open, Pending and Resolved.
optionExplanations.B: The suffix clarifies the state or outcome within its family.
optionExplanations.C: An arbitrary prefix does not inherit resolution semantics.
optionExplanations.D: The application name is not the required category prefix.

quickRecap.value: Communicates where the Case stands; supports reporting/notifications; stored in pyStatusWork.
Standard status table: New, Open, Pending and Resolved. Use descriptive suffixes for more specific states or outcomes.
Explicit Stage/Step configuration controls transition status. The final Stage’s resolution status applies after its Processes complete.
Tell the assignee what to do; appear at runtime on the assignment form.
Status (where it stands) + instructions (what to do) keep users oriented and efficient.
